summary: The requested row contains rowIndex + 1 coefficients, so linear construction time is unavoidable. The binomial recurrence computes and appends each coefficient once.

optimality.argument: For n = rowIndex, the result contains n + 1 coefficients, so materializing it requires Omega(n) time and output storage. The current algorithm starts with the first coefficient and performs one exact recurrence update and one append for each of the remaining n coefficients, giving O(n) time and O(n) returned storage.

replacement_checks.evidence: The required output contains rowIndex + 1 coefficients, which is Theta(rowIndex) for asymptotic analysis.
Each loop iteration derives exactly one new coefficient from its predecessor and appends it to the output.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover the minimum row and nontrivial rows; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
